questions.q: What does executemany() do differently from execute()?
options: It runs the same parameterized statement once per row in a list, in a batch
It only works for SELECT statements
It automatically creates the target table
It ignores parameter placeholders
questions.explain: executemany() batches multiple parameterized inserts far more efficiently than looping with execute().

questions.q: What happens to an INSERT if you close a pyodbc connection without calling conn.commit()?
options: It is saved automatically regardless
It is written but marked inactive
It is silently discarded, since pyodbc connections are not in autocommit mode by default
An exception is always raised immediately
questions.explain: Uncommitted writes sit inside an open transaction and are rolled back when the connection closes.

questions.q: Why do data engineers often write to a staging table instead of directly into a production table?
options: Staging tables are required by SQL Server syntax
So a bad load can be inspected or re-run without touching a table other systems depend on
Production tables cannot accept INSERT statements
Staging tables are always faster to query
questions.explain: A staging table isolates pipeline writes from the tables other systems rely on.

questions.q: In the parameterized INSERT examples in this lesson, what does the ? placeholder represent?
options: A wildcard that matches any column name
A value passed separately from the SQL text, never pasted directly into the string
A comment marker
An optional column that can be skipped
questions.explain: Placeholders keep values separate from SQL syntax, which Lesson 29 explains is also a security requirement.

questions.q: What does TRUNCATE TABLE Staging.ProductSnapshot; accomplish before a load, in this lesson's pattern?
options: It permanently deletes the table definition
It renames the staging table
It empties the staging table so it holds only the current run's data
It backs up the table to a file
questions.explain: Truncating first keeps the staging table from accumulating rows across multiple pipeline runs.
